waves.name: Program dispatcher batch job
waves.rationale: The extractor found no dataset edge for this job, so the seed puts it in the read-only batch family. That label rests on facts the extractor could see. PGMMAIN calls a program named at run time (app/cbl/PGMMAIN.cbl:9), so what the job really reads and writes is bounded only by whatever program it dispatches to. This is a sound first wave only for proving the toolchain on a tiny unit. It is not a proven low-risk wave until the callee set is known.
waves.unblocks: Nothing that the graph shows. There are no shared datasets, copybooks or callers, so on this evidence wave 1 is a chore that proves the toolchain and the equivalence harness. It also forces the answer to what PGMMAIN dispatches to.

unassigned.reason: No static path reaches it, but the computed call at app/cbl/PGMMAIN.cbl:9 could. If the client confirms PGMMAIN dispatches to it, it must move with wave 1, because a port of PGMMAIN without it breaks the dispatch. It stays unplaced until the callee set is bounded.
